name: Ou–Demsky Dependency-Preserving Criterion
description: An execution criterion that forbids out-of-thin-air (OOTA) results by preserving a syntactic notion of dependency, requiring the union of (syntactic) dependency and reads-from to be acyclic. A strictly weaker guarantee than load-store ordering, targeted at Java-like languages in which every memory access can contribute to OOTA. Implemented in the LLVM compiler; the authors measure a 3.1% average (17.6% worst-case) overhead on SPEC CPU2006 for a prototype dependency-preserving compiler.

catSupport.note: acyclic(dep | rf) over syntactic dependencies, which cat exposes as data/addr/ctrl.
